title: Habitat Schoolhouse Preschool — Record Keeping Set (Pond Map + Progress Cards)

pondMap.description: A beautiful watercolor pond scene (frogs, snail, turtle, otter, salamander, duck) with the full alphabet (Aa through Zz) as circles following a winding path from START to END. Six larger circles mark Units 1-6, each featuring a different pond animal. The child marks off each letter circle as they complete it in the workbook. 'Mark off a circle after you complete each letter in Preschool.'
pondMap.value: Turns the abstract concept of 'learning the alphabet' into a visual journey the child can SEE their progress on. The pond map becomes a keepsake — a visual record of their preschool year.

progressCards.description: Six Personal Record cards (Workbook 1 through 6), each with the same 12 developmental skill areas. Each card is filled out at the end of the corresponding workbook. Evaluation key: ✓ Developing Skills, X Needs Development, plus a 'Completed' column.
progressCards.progression: Workbooks 1→5 end with 'Move on to: Preschool Workbook [N+1]'. Workbook 6 ends with 'Register in: Kindergarten with Habitat Schoolhouse'. Clear pathway.
eachCardHas: watercolor animal illustration at top (frog, snail, turtle, otter, salamander, duck)
color-coded background (green, blue, coral, mint, tan, yellow)
progressCards.value: The SAME 12 skills are assessed 6 times across the preschool year. Parent can see growth over time by comparing cards. The mix of academic skills (letter recognition, counting) and life skills (shares, cleans up, seeks help) reflects a whole-child philosophy.

visualProgressTracking.description: The Pond Map turns alphabet learning into a visual journey — a board-game-style path the child colors in as they go. Progress is VISIBLE and TANGIBLE. The child can point to where they are and see how far they've come.
visualProgressTracking.value: Motivation through visual progress. Same psychology as a sticker chart but more beautiful and keepsake-worthy.

repeatedAssessmentAcrossTime.description: The same 12 skill areas assessed 6 times across the year. This isn't 'did they pass/fail' — it's 'are they developing?' The ✓/X key says 'Developing Skills' not 'Mastered.' The framing is growth-oriented, not binary.
repeatedAssessmentAcrossTime.value: Longitudinal development tracking. A parent can see the ARC of their child's growth, not just a snapshot.

wholeChildAssessment.description: The 12 skills mix academic (letter recognition, counting, vocabulary) with social-emotional (shares, works with others, communicates thoughts) and executive function (follows directions, works independently, cleans up). This is a whole-child view, not just academic readiness.
wholeChildAssessment.value: Reflects Charlotte Mason / Reggio / Montessori philosophy: the child's character development matters as much as their academic progress.

watercolorNaturalistAesthetic.description: Every element uses watercolor naturalist illustrations — pond animals (frog, snail, turtle, otter, salamander, duck), watercolor background scenes, botanical elements. Consistent with Carolyng's confirmed preference for this art style.
watercolorNaturalistAesthetic.value: Beautiful enough to be a keepsake. Parents frame these or put them in memory books.

clearPathwayProgression.description: Each workbook card explicitly says 'Move on to: Preschool Workbook [N+1]' until Workbook 6 which says 'Register in: Kindergarten.' The child's educational journey has named waypoints.
clearPathwayProgression.value: Reduces parent anxiety about 'are we on track?' The next step is always clear.

overallLayout.structure: Pond Map = landscape poster; Progress Cards = 2-up per page, portrait
overallLayout.spacing: airy — the pond map has generous space; cards have clean line spacing
overallLayout.flowDirection: pond map: left-right path; cards: top-down checklist

difficulty.complexity: N/A — this is a tracking/assessment tool, not instruction

characters: pond animals: frog, snail, turtle, otter, salamander, duck

printFormat.colorRequirement: needs color — the art is the point

gaps.name: visual-progress-map
gaps.description: A beautiful illustrated map/path showing the child's learning journey. Circles or checkpoints for each letter, number, unit, or milestone. The child marks off progress. Watercolor habitat-themed background. Designed as a keepsake poster.

gaps.name: developmental-progress-card
gaps.description: A periodic assessment card tracking 10-15 whole-child skills (academic + social-emotional + executive function). Same skills assessed repeatedly across the year to show growth. ✓/X evaluation with Completed column. Designed to be filled out at the end of each unit or month.

notes: Third Aless drop. This is a TRACKING and ASSESSMENT system, not instruction. It's the record-keeping layer that sits alongside the workbooks. The Pond Map is particularly interesting for Homa — it's a visual progress tracker that gamifies alphabet learning. The progress cards assess whole-child development (academic + social-emotional + executive function) longitudinally. Combined with Carolyng's earlier directive about uploading completed worksheets to build the learner profile, this suggests BOTH parents value tracking progress over time. Homa could generate both the learning materials AND the progress tracking tools.
